title: Injective module sheaf augmentation on a ringed-site hypercover
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small subcanonical site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; subcanonical means that each presheaf $h_V(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,V)$ is a sheaf. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $W$ be an object of $\mathcal C$ and let $U_\bullet\to W$ be an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], with augmentation commuting with all simplicial operators. Assume it is a hypercover: $h_{U_0}\to h_W$ is an epimorphism of sheaves of sets, and for each $p>0$ the map $h_{U_p}\to M_p$ is an epimorphism, where $M_p$ is the finite limit of the lower-degree representable sheaves giving compatible proper faces of a $p$-simplex over $W$. Define $C^p(U,I)=I(U_p)$ for $p\geq0$, zero for $p<0$, with differential $\delta^p=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j d_j^*$ and $R(W)$-module structure through $U_p\to W$. Then the canonical restriction augmentation $I(W)[0]\to C^\bullet(U,I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $R(W)$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Explicitly the augmented sequence $0\to I(W)\to I(U_0)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}I(U_1)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}I(U_2)\to\cdots$ is exact. No weak contractibility or affineness of the $U_p$ is assumed.

proof.text: For every object $A$ put $P_A(V)=R(V)[\operatorname{Hom}(V,A)]$, the direct sum of copies of $R(V)$ with basis $[a]$, and let $F_A=P_A^\#$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Restrictions send $r[a]$ to $r|_{V\prime}[a|_{V\prime}]$. These are the represented free module presheaves of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], sheafified by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Put $P_p=P_{U_p}$ for $p\geq0$, $P_{-1}=P_W$, $P_{-2}=0$, and $\partial_p=\sum_{j=0}^{p}(-1)^j(d_j)_*$ for $p\geq1$, with $\partial_0$ induced by the augmentation and $\partial_{-1}=0$. The identities $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$ pair the terms with opposite signs in $\partial_{p-1}\partial_p$; augmentation compatibility gives $\partial_0\partial_1=0$. Thus $P_\bullet$, and its sheafification $F_\bullet$, are augmented chain complexes.

proof.text: Fix $V$, an integer $n\geq-1$, and a cycle $z\in P_n(V)$. Its support, together with all iterated faces and their augmentations, gives finite sets $S_k\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(V,U_k)$ for $0\leq k\leq n$ and $S_{-1}\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$ closed under faces (when $n=-1$ just take the support in $S_{-1}$). We construct cones locally, keeping these original sets as labels throughout. For each $w\in S_{-1}$ the epimorphism $h_{U_0}\to h_W$ supplies local lifts $c_{-1}(w)\in h_{U_0}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective]. Make all finitely many choices on a common covering by successively pulling back the next covering to each member of the preceding one and composing coverings, using the axioms of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. No infinite intersection of coverings is taken.

source.place: Tag 01GE, lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves, hypotheses (1)-(3); explicit finite-support cone argument written by NA

proof.text: Inductively assume cones $c_{k-1}$ have been chosen for the labels of degrees below $k$, on each member $V\prime\to V$ of a covering, satisfying $d_0c_{j}(s)=s|_{V\prime}$ and $d_i c_j(s)=c_{j-1}(d_{i-1}s)$ for $i>0$ (in degree zero, $d_0s$ here means augmentation). For $s\in S_k$, prescribe the faces of an element of $h_{U_{k+1}}$ as $b_0=s|_{V\prime}$ and $b_i=c_{k-1}(d_{i-1}s)$ for $1\leq i\leq k+1$. For $0<i<j$, $d_i b_j=c_{k-2}(d_{i-1}d_{j-1}s)=c_{k-2}(d_{j-2}d_{i-1}s)=d_{j-1}b_i$; for $i=0<j$, both sides equal $(d_{j-1}s)|_{V\prime}$. In dimension one their augmentations agree because $c_{-1}$ lifts the augmentation of $s$. These are therefore compatible proper faces over $W$. The finite sheaf matching limit is computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], so this tuple is a matching section. The assumed epimorphism $h_{U_{k+1}}\to M_{k+1}$ and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] lift it locally to $c_k(s)$. Refine finitely many times as in step 2 for all $s\in S_k$. Induction through $k=n$ is finite and establishes the cone identities on a covering of $V$.

source.place: Tag 01GE, lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves; explicit matching-boundary induction written by NA

proof.text: On a final covering member $V\prime$, extend $[s]\mapsto[c_k(s)]$ additively and semilinearly from the free $R(V)$-modules on the ORIGINAL finite label sets $S_k$ to $P_{k+1}(V\prime)$; call these maps $h_k$. Denote restriction on the same labelled modules by $r$. The cone identities give $\partial_{k+1}h_k([s])=[s|_{V\prime}]+\sum_{i=1}^{k+1}(-1)^i[c_{k-1}(d_{i-1}s)]=r([s])-h_{k-1}\partial_k([s])$, hence $\partial h+h\partial=r$. At $k=-1$ the identity is $\partial_0h_{-1}=r$. Since $\partial_n z=0$, $z|_{V\prime}=\partial_{n+1}h_n(z)$. This calculation allows different original labels to restrict to the same simplex: we never define $h$ on the quotient of the labels after restriction. Thus every sectionwise cycle is locally a boundary, in every degree $n\geq-1$, with arbitrary coefficients in $R(V)$.

proof.text: Forget the $R$-action temporarily and apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] with its FIXED ring equal to $\mathbf Z$: it applies to the underlying abelian presheaf complex $P_\bullet$, whose restrictions are group homomorphisms. Its homology presheaf is $V\mapsto\ker\partial_n(V)/\operatorname{im}\partial_{n+1}(V)$, and sheafification commutes with this homology. Step 4 shows that every section of this presheaf becomes zero on a covering. By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] its abelian sheafification has the underlying set sheafification, and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] says every section of that sheaf is locally represented by such presheaf sections. They are locally zero, so separatedness forces the section to be zero. Therefore every homology sheaf vanishes. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the underlying abelian sheaf of $F_A$ is precisely $P_A^\#$; and by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] kernels and sheafified cokernels in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ have the corresponding underlying abelian sheaves. Consequently $\cdots\to F_{U_1}\to F_{U_0}\to F_W\to0$ is exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. The fixed-ring theorem was not applied with the variable ring sheaf $R$.

proof.text: The sheafification adjunction of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] give $\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_A,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(R)}(P_A,I)=I(A)$. Explicitly a morphism corresponds to its value on $[\mathrm{id}_A]$, and its value on $[a:V\to A]$ is the restriction of that section along $a$. Precomposing with $F_{U_{p+1}}\to F_{U_p}$ therefore sends $s\in I(U_p)$ to $\sum_j(-1)^j d_j^*s$; precomposing with $F_{U_0}\to F_W$ gives $I(W)\to I(U_0)$. Thus the dual augmented complex is exactly the one in the statement, including its canonical augmentation.

proof.text: Write $A_{-1}=F_W$ and $A_p=F_{U_p}$, with the differentials of step 5. For $p\geq0$ a dual cocycle $f:A_p\to I$ kills $\operatorname{im}\partial_{p+1}=\ker\partial_p$, so factors uniquely through $\operatorname{im}\partial_p\hookrightarrow A_{p-1}$. Injectivity in [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends this factor to $g:A_{p-1}\to I$. Then $f=g\partial_p$, which is exactly a dual boundary. This also works for $p=0$, when $A_{p-1}=F_W$. Since $\partial_0:A_0\to A_{-1}$ is epi, precomposition $\operatorname{Hom}(A_{-1},I)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A_0,I)$ is injective by the defining cancellation property of an epimorphism. The entire dual augmented sequence is therefore exact.

source.place: Tag 01GW, lemma-injective-trivial-cech, final paragraph; injective Hom argument written explicitly

proof.text: For $a\in R(W)$ and any $s\in I(U_p)$, semilinearity of restrictions gives $d_j^*((a|_{U_p})s)=(a|_{U_{p+1}})d_j^*s$, since the face maps commute with the maps to $W$. The augmentation is $R(W)$-linear for the same reason. For each $A=U_p$ or $W$, with structure map $e_A:A\to W$, define an endomorphism $m_a$ of $P_A$ by $[t:V\to A]\mapsto (a|_{e_A t})[t]$. It is $R(V)$-linear and commutes with restriction, hence sheafifies to an endomorphism of $F_A$. Precomposition with $m_a$ defines the $R(W)$-action on $\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_A,I)$. Evaluating on $[\mathrm{id}_A]$ shows that step 6 identifies this action with multiplication by $a|_A$ on $I(A)$. Exactness of a sequence of modules is equality of the same kernel and image subgroups, so step 7 proves exactness as $R(W)$-modules. Removing the left augmentation gives $H^0(C^\bullet(U,I))\cong I(W)$ via the canonical restriction and $H^p=0$ for $p>0$; negative degrees are zero. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] this is the asserted quasi-isomorphism.
